chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Yusuf ibn al-Harith from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzmī from his father Abd al-Rahman from Ja'far from his father from Jabir from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever catches the Imam on Friday while he is reciting the Tashahhud, let him pray four rak'ahs; and whoever catches one rak'ah, let him add another to it, making it audible."

And that which was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah and al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Friday prayer is not valid except for one who catches both sermons."
So it is interpreted to mean that he does not attain the reward of one who catches both sermons, without it being obligatory upon him to repeat four rak'ahs.
Do you not see what was narrated - Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik who said Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever catches one rak'ah has caught Friday."

So it is explicitly stated in this report that whoever catches one rak'ah has caught Friday; so if the meaning of the first report was not what we mentioned, they would contradict each other, and this is invalid.

And that is because the time for prayer entered before we went out." The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And if the traveler forgets a prayer and remembers it after its time has passed while he is resident, he prays it with reduction (qasar)."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who catches the Friday prayer late and misses the sermons?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between narrations stating that catching one rak'ah suffices for validity and those requiring four rak'ahs by distinguishing between the reward of joining the Imam during the sermons and the obligation to complete the full prayer structure. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the congregational aspect of Jumu'ah, where latecomers must supplement their partial participation with additional voluntary or obligatory units to ensure the prayer's completeness. The text further extends this logic to travelers who miss prayers, emphasizing the principle of Qada (making up) with reduction (Qasr) even after the time has passed.
